simple.meaning: אֶלְגָּבִישׁ (ʼelgâbîysh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “hail (as if a great pearl).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Ezekiel 13:11. The surrounding context includes blood.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אֶלְגָּבִישׁ (H417) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: אֶלְגָּבִישׁ (ʼelgâbîysh) / H417 is traced through Ezekiel 13:11, Ezekiel 13:13, Ezekiel 38:22 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Tell those who plaster it with whitewash that it will fall. There will be an overflowing shower; and you, great hailstones, will fall. A stormy wind will tear it.

majorEvents.evidenceText: I will enter into judgment with him with pestilence and with blood. I will rain on him, and on his hordes, and on the many peoples who are with him, an overflowing shower, with great hailstones, fire, and sulfur.
